description: Combine the current small-shape global leader with the strongest measured n=256 split-graph candidate. Import only the scoped-metadata 2-D sample/task grids, 32-column LD36 initial/middle/final solves, and narrowed shared-address update loaders that reached a 62.592-us floor, preserving all n=512-and-larger winners, caller ordering, caches, fresh inputs, and the full grid.

Merged only fb00acc's scoped batch64/n256 lineage onto the 9eb5fd3 small-shape leader: two-dimensional sample/task grids, scoped factor metadata, LD36 32-column initial/middle/final solves, split final update/factor, and narrowed 32-bit shared-address update loaders. The merge preserved the first parent's n32/n64/n128 paths, every n512-and-larger path, caches, caller queue ordering, and fresh-input behavior. Exactly wrapped build passed; wrapped Modal validation passed all 17 official tests and the six-case fresh-input guard; all 15 active benchmark cells passed. Full-grid geomean measured 760.395 us versus first-parent 756.996 and second-parent 764.863. Exact batch64/n256 measured 66.010 us mean with 62.208 us best, improving the imported parent's 62.592-us clean floor by 0.384 us in this run; n32/n64/n128 measured 16.366/21.192/56.068 us.

Profile-guided Trial1 capped only the dominant n256 initial half-panel stage at 64 registers, targeting the authorized parent profile's 72-register/shared-limited 43.75-percent theoretical occupancy. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, six-case fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Target measured 79.345 us mean/64.012 best versus Trial0 66.010/62.208; aggregate measured 777.772 us versus 760.395, with broad untouched-cell drift and one 3.027-ms target outlier. The clean target floor moved 1.804 us slower, consistent with the lower cap increasing dependency/spill cost rather than repaying an eighth resident block. Restored Trial0's uncapped initial stage and isolated the profile's 19-21-percent excess shared-wavefront target by moving only batch64/n256 graph-update operands from LD72 to aligned LD80. Added a graph-only MathDx GEMM and graph-only shared sizing; legacy n256 factor code and every n512-plus consumer of its LD72 operator remain untouched. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Target measured 66.977 us mean/63.600 best versus Trial0 66.010/62.208, so the wider bank spacing moved the clean floor 1.392 us slower despite remaining stable. Aggregate reached 755.466 us versus Trial0 760.395 and first parent 756.996, driven partly by an unusually low untouched batch8/n2048 mean of 1823.901 us; n32/n64/n128 remained 16.442/21.273/56.197 us. The sole hosted profile slot was already consumed by exact Trial0; no second request launched.

Refined Trial2's LD80 sweep into an asymmetric update layout: only off-diagonal GEMM A operands interpreted column-major use LD80, while B operands, diagonal rank-k updates, and the final update return to proven LD72. A graph-only mixed-LD MathDx operator and paired cp.async offsets preserve all non-target code. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Target measured 66.802 us mean/62.846 best, recovering 0.754 us of Trial2's 63.600 clean floor but remaining 0.638 us above Trial0's 62.208. Aggregate measured 756.912 us versus Trial2 755.466 and Trial0 760.395; n32/n64/n128 held 16.419/21.301/56.365 us. No second hosted profile request launched.

Replaced per-warp sidecar staging in both profiled n256 update nodes with one/two 8-KiB cp.async.bulk transactions and an mbarrier, while compacting graph-only operands to LD64. This cuts update shared memory from 35.84 to 33.00 KiB and replaces 128-256 scalar async-copy instructions per CTA; solves, final update, legacy LD72 paths, caches, and caller ordering remain unchanged. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Target measured 71.184 us mean/66.936 best versus Trial0 66.010/62.208 and Trial3 66.802/62.846. The 4.728-us clean-floor loss shows compact LD64 MathDx bank behavior dominates the staging/footprint savings. Aggregate measured 757.634 us with n32/n64/n128 at 16.396/21.244/56.141 us. No second hosted profile request launched.

Retained Trial4's mbarrier bulk staging but padded the n256 sidecar itself to LD72, making each 9-KiB global tile contiguous so bulk copy could preserve Trial0's proven MathDx bank layout. Wrapped build and all 17 tests plus fresh-input guard passed. The full active benchmark passed cells0-6, with target batch64/n256 at 65.809 us mean/62.708 best versus compact-bulk Trial4 71.184/66.936 and Trial0 66.010/62.208, but unchanged cell7 batch60/n1024 then produced NaN/Inf; eval exited 112 and no complete metric was emitted. The padded global sidecar changes a shared d256 helper/size consumed by the retained batch1024 lineage, so this invalid cross-path coupling will be reset before the next trial. No second hosted profile request launched.

Fixed Trial5's cross-path corruption by keeping the shared d256/batch1024 generic sidecar writer at dense LD64 while padding only graph-specific n256 sidecars and their dedicated initial/middle/final producers/consumers to LD72. Bulk copies now preserve the proven LD72 MathDx layout without touching batch60/n1024. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed, including batch60/n1024 at 914.347 us mean/890.656 best. Target measured 67.917 us mean/62.894 best, recovering 4.042 us from compact-bulk Trial4's 66.936 floor and landing 0.686 us above Trial0's 62.208. Aggregate measured 767.075 amid slow untouched n512/n2048/n4096 cells. No second hosted profile request launched.

The 128-block final solve now drains only its required FP32 output and drops the sidecar argument/conversion; the following 64-block update reloads that committed FP32 panel, converts it directly to LD72 shared half, and proceeds with the unchanged GEMM/POTRF. This removes one 8-KiB global write/read pair and shortens both kernel ABIs while preserving graph order and output semantics. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Initial sidecars remain unchanged. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Initial solves emit only FP32 factor/panels; the first update overlaps direct FP32-to-LD72-half conversion with accumulator cp.async. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Aggregate measured 756.945, helped by unusually fast untouched n32/n512 cells. No second hosted profile request launched.

Returned to Trial7 and replaced the profiled 64-block final update-factor with one cooperative 256-block node: three 32x32x64 LD36 update CTAs store disjoint upper quadrants, fence, and increment per-sample counters; a fourth resident CTA waits, reloads the completed A33, factors/stores it, and resets the counter before kernel completion. The single graph node avoids Trial25's extra launch and uses only 17 KiB shared, with all 256 blocks concurrently resident. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed, proving the in-kernel handoff and replay reset. Target measured 68.719 us mean/65.654 best versus Trial7 65.447/62.320; the 3.334-us clean-floor loss shows duplicated full-panel conversion, atomics, and factor reload outweigh the higher update grid. Aggregate measured 762.498. No second hosted profile request launched.

Refined Trial10's cooperative final node to stage only each quadrant's required 64x32 solved-panel operands in separate LD36 buffers. Diagonal tasks convert one half-panel and alias it for A/B; the off-diagonal task converts both halves, cutting aggregate FP32 loads/conversions across the three update CTAs by one third while preserving the four-CTA handoff and graph-only scope. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Target measured 71.385 us mean/65.722 best with one 1.177-ms outlier versus Trial10 68.719/65.654; the clean floor moved 0.068 us slower, while aggregate measured 768.649 us amid slow untouched n2048 cells. The cooperative kernel's 64x64 factor path still fixes the same 17-KiB shared ceiling. No second hosted profile request launched.

Returned to Trial7 and split its dominant initial node so one 64-block stage factors/stores A00 once, followed by the existing six 32-column solve CTAs reloading that factor instead of recomputing six copies. A graph-only two-source loader preserves source panels, output factor storage, LD36 solves, sidecars, and all non-target paths. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Target measured 82.404 us mean/63.682 best with one 3.742-ms outlier versus Trial7 65.447/62.320; the extra underfilled graph node plus factor store/six reloads moved the clean floor 1.362 us slower despite eliminating five redundant factorizations. Aggregate measured 783.455 us amid a slow untouched n2048 cell. No second hosted profile request launched.

Reworked Trial11's cooperative final node into a three-CTA 32x32 blocked factor DAG. Each CTA retains one rank-64-updated A33 quadrant: task0 factors/stores U00 and publishes state1; task1 reloads U00, solves/stores U01, and publishes state2; task2 reloads U01 as half, applies its Schur update, factors/stores U11, and resets. This removes the fourth CTA, full 64x64 reload/POTRF, and lowers dynamic shared memory from 17 KiB to 13.5 KiB. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Target measured 70.523 us mean/67.562 best versus Trial7 65.447/62.320 and Trial11 71.385/65.722; serialized flag handoffs plus extra 32x32 TRSM/GEMM moved the clean floor 5.242 us behind Trial7. Aggregate measured 757.910 us. The ordinary-grid relaxed-atomic handoffs are B200-validated but remain scheduler-dependent outside the target. No second hosted profile request launched.

Fused Trial13's two final 32-column solve CTAs into its cooperative final node, yielding one five-role 320-block launch with monotonic per-sample state 0-to-2-to-3-to-4-to-0. The two solve producers publish completed U23 halves before the three retained blocked update/POTRF roles, removing one graph launch and full-grid barrier. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed without forward-progress failure. Target measured 75.092 us mean/69.940 best versus Trial13 70.523/67.562 and Trial7 65.447/62.320; removing the launch did not offset forcing every role to reserve 26 KiB shared and adding an initial spin handoff. Aggregate measured 779.877 us amid slow untouched n1024/n2048 cells. The fused ordinary grid raises possible waiting CTAs above the B200 SM count, so its observed progress remains scheduler-dependent. No second hosted profile request launched.

Returned to Trial7 and exposed its block-Cholesky DAG across a persistent side queue. First-update tasks3-5 run beside origin tasks0-2 plus the middle solve, then middle-update task2 runs beside tasks0-1 plus the final solve; captured events join each trailing branch only before its first consumer. Task offsets preserve the exact two-dimensional grids, sidecars, caches, fresh inputs, and caller-origin completion. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Target measured 69.004 us mean/64.488 best versus Trial7 65.447/62.320, recovering 5.452 us of Trial14's 69.940 floor but remaining 2.168 us behind Trial7. Aggregate measured 760.010 us. This capture enqueued each trailing wave before its critical wave, leaving critical-first submission ordering open. No second hosted profile request launched.

Reordered Trial15's captured forks so origin critical updates and their following solve launch before each side-queue trailing wave, retaining identical task splits, events, joins, storage, and caller ordering. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Target measured 82.782 us mean/65.856 best with one 3.400-ms outlier versus Trial15 69.004/64.488 and Trial7 65.447/62.320; even the clean floor moved 1.368 us slower, so critical-first submission did not improve the concurrent schedule. Aggregate measured 787.331 us amid slow untouched n512/n2048 cells. No second hosted profile request launched.

This removes all final FP32-to-FP16 conversion and its LD72 operand but raises dynamic shared memory from about 26 KiB to 34 KiB and trades the mixed-precision GEMM. Wrapped build, all 17 tests, fresh-input guard, and all 15 cells passed. Aggregate measured 772.845 us amid slow untouched n1024/n2048 cells. No second hosted profile request launched.

Graceful return selects Trial33 commit 3a2df5cf2366bf4a45e80e528639b9165108039e: full-grid geomean 755.673 us, batch64/n256 67.582 us mean/61.552 us best, with exactly wrapped build, all 17 tests, the six-case fresh-input guard, and all 15 benchmark cells passing. It improves Trial7's target floor 62.320 by 0.768 us while retaining a near-best aggregate. The numeric aggregate low was Trial23 commit 1392db27000e0a8962a9902f759dea4c721c2cac at 755.448 us, but its target was slower at 70.571/65.776 and its 0.225-us aggregate edge is within broad untouched-cell drift. Across 33 trials this brief measured transposed/padded/bulk sidecars, deferred conversions, cooperative/split/fused update-factor DAGs, side-queue scheduling, FP32 final updates, local factor recomputation fusions, row-owned operand reuse, task-wave ordering, axis interleaving, initial-update fusion, and barrier elimination. The sole authorized hosted profile remains preserved under autocuda/profiles/2026-07-19-01-44-06-cholesky-resumed-local-unmerged/brief-89-trial-0-985e30e6aad26390564900a5c2c723b3acea693d.*; no additional profile request was made. If a follow-up brief resumes this line, concrete openings include fusing paired output stores with next-accumulator cp.async on Trial33, testing the remaining balanced task-wave permutations, or combining its barrier-safe row pairing with a distinct middle-update schedule.
